name: Classic Inca Trail to Machu Picchu
why: Four days on the Incas' own stone path, through cloud forest and ruins nobody else sees, to enter Machu Picchu through the Sun Gate at dawn.
book: Only with a licensed operator, and permits are limited per day: book 4-6 months ahead for May-September. Closed every February for maintenance. Bring your passport.
water: Your operator boils water at camp; buy bottles at the last village on day 1.
dangers: Dead Woman's Pass at 4,215 m: arrive with 2-3 days in Cusco first.
Endless stone steps on day 3: knees and poles.
Rain from November to March; the trail is muddy and the views close.
turnaround: Your guide sets the pace; the group must reach Wiñay Wayna on night 3.

points.name: Km 82, Piscacucho bridge
points.note: Day 1: permit and passport check, then the suspension bridge over the Urubamba and an easy valley walk past Llactapata (Patallacta).

points.name: Wayllabamba
points.note: Night 1: the last village on the trail, at about 3,000 m; some groups camp an hour higher at Ayapata.

points.name: Dead Woman's Pass (Warmiwañusca)
points.note: Day 2: the hardest climb, about 1,200 m up to 4,215 m, the highest point of the trail.

points.name: Pacaymayo camp
points.note: Night 2: the camp at about 3,600 m in the valley below the pass; cold at night.

points.name: Wiñay Wayna terraces
points.note: Day 3: past Runkurakay, Sayacmarca and Phuyupatamarca to the biggest ruins of the trail, by the last camp.

points.name: Inti Punku, the Sun Gate
points.note: Day 4: up the steep 'gringo killer' steps before dawn; Machu Picchu appears below.

points.name: Machu Picchu
points.note: Another hour down past small ruins into the citadel, through the guardhouse terraces.
